name: What is the difference between porcelain and ceramic tile for kitchen floors?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between porcelain and ceramic tile for kitchen floors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain tile is generally the preferred choice for kitchen flooring due to its exceptional durability and moisture resistance. Porcelain is fired at higher temperatures than ceramic, making it denser, less porous, and highly resistant to stains, heavy foot traffic, and dropped items. Ceramic tile is slightly softer and easier to cut, which can make it a budget-friendly option for light-traffic areas or decorative vertical backsplashes. However, for active kitchen floors subject to spills, moisture, and pet claws, porcelain tile provides superior long-term performance and lower maintenance demands.
acceptedAnswer.description: Porcelain tile is denser, more water-resistant, and harder wearing than ceramic, making it the better choice for high-traffic kitchen floors prone to spills.
